verdicts.quote: **earn** is the more usual word in writing
verdicts.reason: This is not generally true: make is also common in writing, especially for a business's profit or revenue and for stated pay.

verdicts.quote: The clause after **make sure** takes the present simple for future time: *make sure you are there at six*, not *will be there*.
verdicts.reason: A future form is possible after make sure, especially where the clause reports an expected future situation, as in “Make sure you will be there at six.”
Make good on is also established in British English, though it may be less frequent there, so an American-only regional label is misleading.

reviewers.summary: The entry is broadly accurate and learner-usable. Correct the sense 6 grammar code and the inaccurate claims about earn in writing, future will after make sure, and the American-only label for make good on.
